source_document.body:
Knight-Swift Transportation is benefitting from its high exposure to one-way truckload, the portion of the market experiencing the largest gains from the regulatory-fueled capacity shakeout. The carrier said Wednesday, in conjunction with its better-than-expected third-quarter report , that its tender rejections and spot rates are well ahead of industry averages, allowing it to quickly restore margins.
“On the pricing front, our spot pricing trended better than public indicators in the quarter, staying well above contractual rates that continued to accelerate throughout the period,” said CEO Adam Miller in a news release. “Similarly, our tender rejection rates continue to run at levels two to three times that of the broader market measures.”
SONAR: Outbound Tender Rejection Index (OTRI.USA) for 2026 (blue shaded area), 2025 (yellow line), 2024 (green line) and 2023 (pink line). A proxy for truck capacity, the tender rejection index shows the number of loads being rejected by carriers. Current tender rejections show a tight truckload market. To learn more about SONAR, click here .
Knight-Swift ( NYSE: KNX ) reported third-quarter adjusted earnings per share of 83 cents Wednesday after the market closed. The result was 51 cents higher than the year-ago quarter and 7 cents better than analysts’ expectations. (Management’s EPS guidance range was 71 to 77 cents.)
Revenue of $2.2 billion was up 14% year over year (plus-8% y/y excluding fuel surcharges) and slightly ahead of the $2.17 billion consensus estimate.
Table: Knight-Swift’s key performance indicators – Consolidated
TL margins turn the corner
The company’s TL unit reported a 6.5% y/y revenue increase, excluding fuel. Revenue per tractor (ex-fuel) was up 11% y/y while the average tractor count was down 4%.
Knight-Swift has been culling its truck fleet through the downturn to improve asset utilization. Loaded miles per tractor increased 1%, which was an eighth straight y/y improvement. Deadhead was down 170 basis points y/y to 12.1%. Revenue per loaded mile (ex-fuel) increased 10% y/y. (The metric was up by a mid-teen percentage in its over-the-road service.)
Table: Knight-Swift’s key performance indicators – Truckload
An 89.2% adjusted operating ratio (inverse of operating margin ) was 700 bps better y/y and in line with the midpoint of management’s guidance range. U.S. Xpress, which was acquired in 2023 , operated at a low-90% adjusted OR in the quarter while Knight-Swift’s legacy brands operated at 88%. Management noted that one-way margins exceeded dedicated margins in the period. (Approximately 29% of Knight-Swift’s TL fleet operates under dedicated contracts.)
The carrier is meaningfully pricing freight above cost inflation. During the first quarter, an increase in revenue per total mile (ex-fuel) lagged the increase in cost per mile (net of fuel surcharges) by 90 bps. The spread flipped to 390 bps positive in the second quarter, with rate gains outpacing cost inflation by 840 bps in the third quarter.
The company is again calling for 650 to 750 bps of y/y TL margin improvement in the fourth quarter, implying an 85.9% adjusted OR (330 bps better sequentially). Its guidance also calls for revenue to increase y/y by a low-double-digit percentage (ex-fuel).
It said it will look to selectively grow the fleet, but acknowledged “sourcing quality drivers is as challenging as it has been in years.” Knight-Swift’s new bid season kicks off next month and it will ask for “at least double-digit [rate] increases” for starters, Miller said on Wednesday evening call with analysts.
“I think we’ll start the bid season with the idea of probably low-to-mid double digits and see how it develops from there.”
SONAR: Van Contract Rate Per Mile Index ( VCRPM1.USA ) for 2026 (blue shaded area), 2025 (yellow line), 2024 (green line) and 2023 (pink line). The index shows a 7-day moving average of the initial reporting of dry van contract rates without fuel or accessorial charges.
National LTL map may be completed organically
Knight-Swift entered the less-than-truckload market in 2021 when it acquired AAA Cooper . It added Midwest Motor Express later that year and Dependable Highway Express in 2024 . It has opened over 50 locations organically over the past five years, including four new locations in May.
However, it still needs to fill in the Northeast portion of the map to complete a true national network. It said Wednesday it has already chosen a few locations in the region and plans to add terminals organically at a “very deliberate” pace.
Table: Knight-Swift’s key performance indicators – Less-than-truckload
Revenue at the unit was up less than 1% y/y (ex-fuel) as tonnage increased 3% and revenue per hundredweight (ex-fuel) fell 1%. Increases in weight per shipment (+5%) and length of haul (+6%) had mostly offsetting impacts on yield.
Revenue per shipment (ex-fuel) increased 4% y/y. Contractual rate renewals were up by a mid-single-digit percentage.
The LTL unit booked a 91.4% adjusted OR, 80 bps worse y/y. A $4.6-million decline in gains on sale was a 130-bp y/y margin headwind.
The company’s fourth-quarter outlook calls for a high-single- to low-double-digit y/y increase in revenue (ex-fuel), with 100 to 200 bps of y/y margin improvement, implying a 93.6% OR at the midpoint of the range.
Other Q3 takeaways
The logistics unit reported 120 bps of y/y margin improvement to a 93.1% adjusted OR. Brokerage gross margin increased 110 bps y/y to 18.9% (350 bps better sequentially) as the company “maintained a disciplined approach to profitability and carrier selection.”
The intermodal unit booked a second straight operating profit (97.8% adjusted OR). Load counts increased 13% y/y to the highest level in over five years and revenue per load was 15% higher (up 5.5% y/y ex-fuel).
Table: Knight-Swift’s key performance indicators – Logistics & Intermodal
Knight-Swift issued fourth-quarter adjusted EPS guidance of 78 to 84 cents, which bracketed the 82-cent consensus estimate at the time of the print.
The third-quarter adjusted EPS number benefitted y/y from a $22-million reduction in net interest expense (10 cents per share), a lower tax rate (5 cents per share) and a slight increase in gains on equipment sales (1 cent per share). However, the other income line was down $3.5 million y/y (2 cents per share).
Why it matters? Knight-Swift is the nation’s largest asset-based TL carrier and serves as a bellwether for market trends. The company’s third-quarter results highlight that the market has transitioned from a cyclical downturn to a structural recovery.

Ford opened orders for the 2027 Mustang Mach-E , which now offers a standard extended-range battery for under $40,000. A new Trail model is also joining the lineup.
2027 Ford Mustang Mach-E prices and range
Ford’s electric crossover SUV is back for another model year. The 2027 Mustang Mach-E drops the standard-range battery offered in the 2026 model and now comes standard with the larger 88 kWh battery.
The 2027 Ford Mustang Mach-e is available in five trims: Select, Premium, GT, Rally, and a new purpose-built Trail model.
The new 2027 Ford Mustang Mach-E Trail is available for a $2,295 package upgrade for the Select eAWD.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
According to Ford, the new Trail package is designed to make “outdoor adventures across pavement, gravel, and dirt roads more accessible than ever.”
It features fine-tuned front and rear struts and springs, a Rally-shaped steering rack, 10-inch High Gloss Dark Carbonized Gray Wheels with as-cast graphics, and is 10 mm taller in the front and 15 mm taller in the rear than the base Mach-E.
2027 Ford Mustang Mach-E Trail (Source: Ford)
The 2027 Mustang Mach-E Trail comes with standard 400W, 12V Pro Power Onboard. It’s available as an upgrade for other variants, including the Premium, GT, and Mustang Mach-E Rally.
Select and Premium models use the 88 kWh battery and are available with rear- or all-wheel-drive (eAWD) powertrains. The GT and Rally variants use the 91 kWh battery and are only sold as eAWD models.
2027 Ford Mustang Mach-E Trail (Source: Ford)
Ford’s BlueCruise 1.5 comes standard on the GT and Rally and optional on Select with Tech Pack Lite and Premium with Premium Tech Pack models. The Trail requires the hardware selection at the time of ordering. It cannot be added later.
Meanwhile, the Ford Connectivity Package and Ford Security Package are standard across the entire 2027 lineup.
2027 Ford Mustang Mach-E Trail interior (Source: Ford)
The base 2027 Ford Mustang Mach-E Select RWD starts at $39,995. Including the $2,045 destination fee, prices start at $42,040.
While it is a bit more expensive than the 2026 model year, Ford no longer offers the standard-range battery. Ford said a new secondary front motor delivers the same performance as the previous unit but at a lower cost, enabling the lower-priced base RWD model with the extended-range battery.

Tesla Stock Falters Despite Better-Than-Expected Q3 Earnings, It's Still a Carmaker

Photo: Tesla
Tesla's third-quarter results failed to impress Wall Street, despite showing a sound financial position and promising prospects. Free cash flow and capex spending beat Wall Street estimates, even though profitability took a hit. However, the silver lining is that Tesla is again expected to grow its vehicle sales, with plans to increase production capacity to 5 million vehicles by 2030.
Coming right after SpaceX's earnings call on Tuesday, Tesla's earnings call produced a lukewarm reaction even among the company's biggest fans. Everyone was in agreement that SpaceX has produced a much more consistent performance than Tesla, even though Elon Musk headed both calls. Unsurprisingly, even though Tesla had a lot to brag about, the stock fell more than 5% after closing.
The good news was that Tesla beat Wall Street estimates as far as free cash flow and capex spending are concerned. The reported free cash flow was $1.53 billion against estimates of -$4.92 billion. At the same time, capital expenditures were lower than expected, at $4.732 billion vs $7.96 billion for the quarter. Tesla now expects full-year capex to top at $20 billion instead of the previously guided $25 billion.
The third-quarter revenue came in flat, at $28.046 billion vs $28.095 billion in 2025, slightly below analyst consensus of about $28.13 billion. Automotive revenue in the quarter dropped 3% to $20.560 billion from 2025, while Energy generation and storage saw an unexpected 16% drop to $2.881 billion. The bright spot was in the services department, which ballooned 33% in the quarter to $4.605 billion. Supercharger, insurance, and parts sales were cited as the main contributors.
Photo: Tesla These numbers are useful to investors who want to see how Tesla is navigating through so many storms, including geopolitical risks, tariffs, and supply chain disruptions. However, they don't tell the whole story, which is why the earnings call is such a useful tool to both media and investors. As disappointing as the Q3 earnings call was for some, it still provided great information about Tesla's plans.
Since I'm a car guy, I am mostly excited about Tesla's announced plans to expand its vehicle manufacturing capacity. This was rather surprising, considering that Tesla hasn't maxed out its current capacity yet. During the call, Elon Musk announced that Tesla aims for 5 million vehicles per year by 2030. Could this be a sign that it plans new vehicle models?
Tesla also announced that it reached 1.74 million active FSD subscriptions in Q3 2026. Musk said that over 75% of new vehicles are ordered with a paid FSD subscription. This made him believe that people are now "buying FSD with a car attached, not the other way around."
Musk also announced that Unsupervised FSD should roll out in the second quarter of 2027 with FSD V15. When this happens, Tesla owners in geofenced areas will be able to enroll their cars in the Robotaxi network. Tesla Robotaxi app has already included strings to implement such a feature, as decompiled software revealed. Bare Necessities: 2027 Go Play 17DBS Sport Might Be the Best Deal for Big Families and New RV Owners
21 photos
Photo: Josh the RV Nerd at Bish's RV | YouTube Screenshot
A recent study completed by RVIA mentions that Americans are still placing affordability above all other RV and camper traits. So, with that in mind, I've decided to bring to light a camper that gives American families all they need and nothing else, and all at a price that really surprised me.
Folks, Wayfinder RV showcases a starting price tag of just $17,500 for the 2027 Go Play 17DBS Sport, this brands latest and most-equipped layout that’s aimed at the entry level RV owner, and if I may, I was actually blown away with the number of features that this brand managed to stuff into the trailer.
As mentioned, this is an entry level unit and for the price tag that it carries, we’re looking at a “stick and tin” construction with a wooden frame and painted aluminum exterior. While it’s not the sort of construction that’ll last you ages, with proper love and care, some can see up to 15 years of use.
Photo: Josh the RV Nerd at Bish's RV | YouTube Screenshot While it may not be the most feature-filled option on the market, nor one that calls upon the most prime of materials, it does offer ample space for larger families to get out there and, well, “Go Play,” in particular, outside, as there isn’t much to do inside but sleep, lounge around, cook and eat, and escape bad weather.
For a general feeling of the layout, allow me to point out that at the very front of the unit, Wayfinder decided to add a residential 60x80-inch queen mattress with storage options underneath and above. The AC hovers above and sticks out into the interior, so watch your head.
This is where two people will be able to rest their heads at night, maybe even three if a small child is in there, and another two kids or adults will be catching Zs on the modular U-shaped dinette. That’s four to five guests so far and while most people would feel that this is about the limit in this price bracket, it isn’t, with Wayfinder stuffing two double bunks into the rear of the 17DBS.
Photo: Josh the RV Nerd at Bish's RV | YouTube Screenshot Josh, the host in the video below does point out a peak of 600 lbs (272 kg) per bunk. Plen-ty and quite the sleeping capacity for something that costs as much as some teardrop campers I've written about this year, and there’s still a bit more to go over.
Since this isn’t the biggest camper in the world, rolling in with a length of a bit over 23.5 ft (7.2 m), and most of the space inside is occupied by the beds, it leaves little room for a complete bathroom or massive kitchen where you can cook up a storm .
For example, the bathroom, while completed with a separate toilet and shower, doesn’t include a sink, so you’ll have to wash your hands elsewhere, nor does it include a powered vent, so you’ll need to be sure to air things out very well or go for an upgrade.
Photo: Josh the RV Nerd at Bish's RV | YouTube Screenshot As for the kitchen, it’s there, and ready with a fridge that’s decently sized for a group this large, doesn’t include much countertop space to work with for meal preps. You'll need to use a sink cover to do so as the cooktops do stick out of the countertop. There’s a microwave inside too.
Our stays are also supported with features like a tankless water heater, 19K BTU furnace, the AC I mentioned, ample lighting, and 30 gals of freshwater. Do keep in mind that this makes up for a camper that weighs 4,800 lbs (2,177 kg) GVWR, so be sure your vehicle can tow this much. Some SUVs can, placing this RV option on the radar of vehicle owners that don’t just have trucks.
Cargo-carrying capacity does stand at nearly 1,070 lbs (485 kg), but if you add any upgrades, you’ll start to diminish that number for toys, gear, and other essentials.
Now, I stumbled across this unit in a video from Josh the RV Nerd at Bish’s RV (Hat-tip to you folks!) and in it, he does showcase what this camper’s “road mode” is like. If I may, I was surprised to see that we can access every single space inside this one while it’s scrunched up for the road.
Photo: Josh the RV Nerd at Bish's RV | YouTube Screenshot The bunks can be accessed, the bedroom too, the bathroom, and you can still whip up a sandwich or grab a change of clothes. What you can’t do, according to Josh, is use the dinette be it for sitting, sleeping, or “human bouncing.” The dinette cushions also don’t have a particular way to keep them in place and not bounce around while you drive.
What I'd personally like to point out is that the spec sheet mentions that solar is NA, so you’ll clearly need to go the full mile in terms of upgrades and gear to tap into free power, or optionally, you can opt for a portable power station with internal inverter and a set of solar panels. Some dealers will install solar for you, for an extra buck, of course.
Oh, and last but not least, keep in mind that some dealers are selling this a bit under the MSRP, sometimes, adding a minor upgrade or two here and there, so take the time to shop around, not to mention making then ‘fight’ over your money; disrupt the system.
Frankly, it appears as though Wayfinder is about to sell some 2027 Go Play 17DBS Sport travel trailers.

2027 Yamaha MT-125 Remains a True Hyper Naked, Adds More of the Urban Twist
58 photos
Photo: Yamaha
Facelifts are a common thing in the auto industry, but not as much in the moto one. Whereas for carmakers the term means applying design modifications that are immediately noticeable, as far as motorcycles are concerned, a facelift only refers to fresh paint jobs and graphics being added to the offering. Well, here's Yamaha with a facelift that contradicts all of the above.
The Japanese bike maker announced this week the launch of the new version of the MT-125 hyper naked for the 2027 model year, packing a new look (that was achieved not only through new colors, but actual, physical changes as well) meant to bring it in line with that of its siblings from the MT family (MT-09, MT-07, and MT-03), but also to give it an even more urban look.
What Yamaha did was change the shape of the fuel tank, giving it more sculpted and aggressive lines, go for fresh side fairings with a transparent dark smoke glitchy pattern and the MT logo, and fit a redesigned, stretched seat.
The new MT-125 also makes use of blade-style position LED lights, LED indicators, and a revised headlight so that it looks different than it used to even when riding at night.
Wrapping everything up is, how else, a new paint scheme, a high-contrast one that includes Redline White (with or without a two-tone seat). This one joins the already available Ice Storm, Icon Blue, and Tech Black.
Mechanically speaking, the motorcycle stays true to the setup that has made it famous. That would be the 125cc engine sitting in the Deltabox frame, 41 mm upside-down forks at the front to hold it upright, and an 810 m high seat to hold the rider.
The hyper naked ships complete with a five-inch TFT display that can support smartphone connectivity (the Yamaha MyRide app is required for that) and allows access to turn-by-turn navigation.
Yamaha says that this latest incarnation of a two-wheeler that first saw daylight more than a decade ago will hit European shores in the first quarter of next year. The bike maker makes no mention of cost, meaning you'll have to get in touch with your local dealer to learn more about that.
As for the American market, the MT hyper naked family there doesn't list the 125 as one of the options. Six-model strong at the time of writing, the American lineup consists of the MT-03, MT-07, MT-09, and MT-10 – these final two accompanied by their SP variants.
For the record, the cheapest Yamaha hyper naked that can be had on the American market is the $4,999 MT-03, while at the opposite end sits the MT-10 SP, which sells for $17,499 in its 2026 model year incarnation.

Mercedes-Benz CTO Joerg Burzer Says Gasoline and Electric Mercedes-AMG C 63 Are in the Works
16 photos
Photo: Mercedes-AMG
Few peeps actually wanted the most powerful C-Class ever built. Rated at 671 horsepower and tremendous peak torque from a 2.0-liter turbo inline-four mill and plug-in assistance for good measure, the outgoing C 63 outpunches the V8 model it replaces. Even so, it still bombed so badly that AMG executives have spent years admitting weak demand in public.
The folks in Affalterbach called it progress, but customers viewed the plug-in hybrid C 63 more as an appliance. Following the German automaker's long-awaited mea culpa, chief technical officer Joerg Burzer made it clear that AMG is now developing two distinct C 63 models.
Speaking to Australia's Drive, he confirmed that one would be powered by dinosaur juice as opposed to electricity for the other. That's exactly what BMW is doing with the M3. Over in Munich, the M division is putting the finishing touches on the first-ever M3 with electric-only propulsion while also working behind the scenes on what some have described as the final M3 with internal combustion.
Although Burzer wouldn't confirm what hides under the hood of the internal combustion C 63's replacement, the four-cylinder turbo dies regardless. Euro 7 and poor demand killed it, and Mercedes won't spend a single cent to keep it alive. Not only does an I4 seem out of place in such a vehicle, but a small four straining for V8-grade output runs way too hot and generates way too much NOx.
An inline-six turbo with mild-hybrid goodies and the C 53 moniker should move in as the indirect replacement of the plug-in C 63. The GLC 63 already runs a 3.0-liter unit with 48-volt assistance, so pencil in 443 horsepower and 443 pound-feet (600 Newton-meters) of twist. An overboost function should increase peak torque to 472 pound-feet (640 Newton-meters) for 10 seconds at a time.
Photo: SH Proshots What about the possibility of a V8? Burzer laughed at that idea even though the platform underpinnings the C-Class supports V8 muscle in the CLE and larger models. Burzer may have laughed it off, but also kept the door cracked by mentioning an "exciting future ahead of us." Reading between the lines, the C 63 with V8 muscle could return with the next generation of the C-Class.
Certifying an eighter into a freshly redesigned compact luxury sedan never made financial sense in the first place, so yeah, the next C 63 will have to wait a bit. Its electric brother is not waiting for anything. Spy photographers keep catching the zero-emission model in Germany, and the most recent of prototypes appear to feature production-intent body panels and exterior lighting units.
While its biggest rival may feature quad motors, AMG has a trick up its sleeve in the form of axial-flux motor technology. The axial-flux design has been repeatedly proven by a bunch of automakers, including Ferrari and Lamborghini. The GT 4-Door Coupe and its SUV-bodied sib already pull 1,153 horsepower from three of them, and the electric CLA 45 boasts 671 horsepower from three as well.
This information alone suggests that AMG has decided on three units for the C 63 with EQ Technology, with its maximum output estimated in the 800-hp region. To recap, the six-cylinder AMG C 53 and three-motor C 63 with EQ Technology will have to suffice until Mercedes drops a completely new internal combustion C 63 worthy of this badge in the 2030s.

Joint Typhoon Warning Center
By Alexander Whiteman
22 October 2026
Congestion may be easing in eastern China, but with Typhoon Champi set to sweep across the north-east coast of Taiwan tomorrow there are concerns that disruption to vessel movements could undo benefits carriers are seeing in China.
Maersk told customers waiting times at ports along the east China coast were showing a continued week-on-week decline, with its wider east Asian network stabilising following disruption from earlier typhoons.,
The carrier said: “Recovery efforts across East Asia continue to progress, although strong export demand is putting pressure on congested ports. Operational conditions at East China ports have improved. Vessel wait times have continued to decline.
“While the direct impact of recent typhoon activity has largely subsided, recovery across the wider regional network remains ongoing. Conditions across the port network continue to influence overall cargo flows and schedule recovery.”
Maritime services provider Mas Oceans is, however, warning that fresh adverse weather associated with Typhoon Champi could create “further operational challenges”, with reports that pilotage at the Changjiang Estuary had been suspended.
Furthermore, there have been restrictions on vessel movements at some ports, with anticipated closures affecting Zhejiang, Fujian, and surrounding areas if the typhoon matches forecast severity, raising the prospect of renewed delays.
Chantal Roberts, director of Drewry Supply Chain Advisors, said if a port was forced out of operation for even a day, “you need around five weeks in a quiet period, or about two months in a peak period, to really clear that backlog”.
The extent of any typhoon-induced disruption will depend on how long restrictions remain in place, the number of vessels affected and how quickly terminals can clear backlogs once operations resume.
And, if the threat of a typhoon was not enough, Maersk noted it was likely intermittent delays would continue along its East Asia network, adding that it was “monitoring conditions and contacting customers whose shipments might be affected” to discuss available options.
Elsewhere, the Danish carrier sailed nearly double the number of vessels through the Suez Canal over the nine months to October as it did during the same period last year, according to figures from the Suez Canal authority.
With a total of 23.3m tonnes moved through the besieged waterway this year, compared with 7m last year, Maersk chief operating officer Rabab Boulos told the authority the group hoped to return all its services to the canal by March.

By Alex Lennane
22 October 2026
Semiconductor and cloud infrastructure shipments helped drive almost 10% growth in Kuehne + Nagel’s third-quarter airfreight volumes, contrasting with falling tonnage at rival DSV, as it pruned accounts and managed Schenker integration effects.
K+N handled 619,000 tonnes in Q3, up 9.8% year on year, with growth accelerating from 2.8% in Q2. Air Logistics net turnover rose 38%, to CHF2.4bn ($2.9bn), while EBIT increased 84%, to CHF169m.
Its results presentation identified semiconductors and cloud infrastructure as key growth drivers alongside general hard cargo, and highlighted export strength from South-east Asia, excluding China.
Gross profit per 100kg was broadly stable, quarter on quarter, while unit costs edged lower. The division’s conversion ratio increased to 32.4%, from 22.8% a year earlier.
The benefits of hi-tech demand extended beyond airfreight; K+N reported rising demand from the sector in Road Logistics, while recent investment in hi-tech sector growth was also helping improve Contract Logistics earnings.
The performance contrasts with DSV, which yesterday reported a 3% decline in both air and sea freight volumes. Growth in technology business in APAC and North America partly offset weaker European activity, reduced ecommerce volumes, and other pressures.
DSV also attributed part of its airfreight decline to deliberate yield-management measures. CEO Jens Lund told analysts around two percentage points of the 3% reduction reflected the “sanitising” of accounts.
The contrasting performances highlight the importance of maintaining commercial momentum during acquisitions. K+N is reporting volume and market share gains, while DSV is working to stabilise its underlying business as it integrates Schenker.
Jefferies analysts described K+N’s results as “another beat and raise”, attributing the improvement to strong volume growth, yields, and cost control. Their assessment of DSV focused on stabilisation of the underlying business, allowing acquisition synergies to drive earnings growth.
Investors nevertheless welcomed DSV’s results, sending its shares up 15.1% yesterday to DKr1,381.50, from DKr1,200 the previous day – although they remained well below February’s DKr1,900+.
K+N’s reaction was more muted: its shares were trading 0.7% higher, at CHF231.50, at 10.55am UK time today, following its results and upgraded outlook.
Across K+N, Q3 net turnover rose 22% year on year, to CHF7.4bn, while EBIT increased 53%, to CHF435m, and earnings rose 53%, to CHF316m.
The group raised its full-year recurring EBIT guidance to CHF1.5bn–1.6bn, from CHF1.35bn–1.55bn, lifting the midpoint by CHF100m.
Sea Logistics volumes increased 4.5%, to 1.16m teu, supported by market share gains on ex-Asia and transatlantic routes. Divisional EBIT rose 55%, to CHF172m, with yields improving 5% quarter on quarter.
Road Logistics net turnover increased 14%, while EBIT grew 40%, to CHF28m. Contract Logistics EBIT rose 7%, to CHF66m, although new customer projects required upfront investment and the addition of around 4,000 employees. The division had 37 new contracts in implementation.
Alongside growth from customers’ technology investment, K+N reaffirmed its expectation of an AI-related uplift of CHF100m–150m emerging from 2027.
That remains separate from its broader cost reduction programme, which it said was ahead of schedule, and was expected to contribute more than CHF150m in gross savings this year.
The presentation provided no further breakdown of the AI applications or measured productivity gains underpinning the target.

Kia’s electric sports car beat out the Tesla Model Y Performance and BYD’s Sealion 7 in a recent comparison test by the German magazine Auto Motor und Sport , ranking first overall.
Kia EV6 GT takes first in German performance EV test
It wasn’t a German brand or a Chinese one. It wasn’t even the Tesla Model Y Performance. Kia’s electric sports car, the EV6 GT, took first place in a recent high-performance EV test in Germany, the heart of Europe.
The comparison test, held by German auto magazine Auto Motor und Sport , evaluated five high-performance EVs across seven categories: body, safety, comfort and convenience, powertrain, driving performance, environmental friendliness, and running costs.
The EV6 GT ranked first overall with 585 points, 9 points ahead of the Tesla Model Y Performance, which took second with 576 points.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The Zeekr 7GT ranked third with 569 points, followed by the Polestar 4 Coupe Dual Motor with 531 points, and the BYD Sealion 7 AWD Excellence, which ranked fifth with 508 points.
Kia’s electric sports car took the top spot in three of the seven categories: safety, powertrain, and driving performance. In the safety category, the EV6 GT scored highest for its superior braking and high-speed stability.
Kia EV6 GT (Source: Kia Germany)
The EV6 GT earned praise in the powertrain category, boasting up to 650 horsepower and 770 Nm of torque from its dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain.
In the driving performance category, Kia’s electric sports car scored 20 points higher (96 points) than the Tesla Model Y Performance in second (76 points).
According to Auto Motor und Sport, the Kia EV6 GT took first place overall in the comparison test due to its “outstanding driving performance.”
Performance is one thing, but it also stands out with fun features, including Virtual Gear Shift. Borrowed from the Hyundai IONIQ 5 N, the feature simulates the feeling and sounds of a six-speed paddle-operated transmission.
Kia overhauled the interior for the newest model with its new connected car Navigation Cockpit (ccNC) infotainment system.
Kia EV6 GT interior (Source: Kia Germany)
The new system includes dual 12.3″ navigation and driver display screens in a curved panoramic setup.
Kia’s electric sports car can sprint from 0 to 100 km/h (0 to 62 mph) in 3.5 seconds. It uses a new 84 kWh battery, providing a WLTP range of up to 279 miles.
With 800V fast-charging capabilities, the Kia EV6 GT can recharge from 10% to 80% in as little as 18 minutes.
In Germany, the new Kia EV6 GT starts at 69,990 euros ($78,000). The Tesla Model Y Performance, on the other hand, starts at 63,970 euros in Germany. It offers a WLTP range of up to 360 miles (580 km) and accelerates from 0 to 100 km/h (0 to 62 mph) in 3.5 seconds.
Which high-performance EV would you drive? The Kia EV6 GT or the Tesla Model Y Performance? Let us know in the comments.
Unfortunately, Kia said it was discontinuing the EV6 GT in the US “until further notice” earlier this year.

© Jorg Hackemann
By Ian Putzger Americas correspondent
22 October 2026
After the US lifted restrictions on Mexican airlines launching routes from the capital to the northern neighbour, several have signalled ambitions to avail themselves of the opportunity.
With restrictions on US airlines also removed and moves by the Mexican government to beef up aviation, cross-border traffic appears poised for expansion.
The US-Mexico aviation dispute took a large step towards resolution last week when Washington announced the end of its sanctions on Mexican airlines imposed in July of last year after taking umbrage at the government’s decision in 2023 to ban freighters from Mexico City’s Benito Juarez airport (AICM) and curtail take-off slots at the chronically congested airport – steps the US authorities deemed a violation of their aviation bilateral agreement.
Faced with the prospect of having its aviation safety downgraded once again to Category 2, the Mexican authorities have largely yielded to US demands for restitution of landing slots at AICM taken from US passenger airlines. They also took a step back on the freighter ban.
The Secretariat of Infrastructure, Communication and Transport stated that freighter operations would be permitted during times when AICM is not congested and that US carriers would be welcome to apply. In return, Washington gave the green light for new Mexican airline flights from AICM and Felipe Angeles Airport (AIFA), the Mexican capital’s designated freighter gateway.
According to the Mexican transport ministry, 10 to 12 new routes could be launched in a first phase, mostly from AIFA, where operating capacity is available.
Mexico’s National Chamber of Air Transport said it was “a significant step to offer certainty to the industry and advance actions that help the development of passenger and cargo services”.
Robert Van De Weg, CEO of Mexican cargo airline mas, commented: “In general it is a positive signal that things are opening up,” but added that he did not expect this to trigger an immediate surge in activity in the market.
So far, US passenger and cargo airlines have not given any official signs of plans to resume flights to AICM or AIFA. Their Mexican counterparts on the passenger side appear more anxious to start new US flights.
Aeromexico CEO Andres Conesa told reporters on Tuesday it was considering several US destinations and a first batch of routes could be launched early next year, with potentially more halfway through 2027. He did not disclose destinations, except San Juan, which would likely be started in the second tranche, he said.
The first batch of new routes could be unveiled as early as next week, he added, and his finance chief, Ricardo Sanchez, indicated that Aeromexico had aircraft available to mount new flights.
Volaris commented that the regulatory development would allow it to advance connectivity between Mexico City and US destinations, while Viva indicated that it would begin to evaluate possible routes.
But Mexican cargo airlines have not voiced any plans for new US-bound flights, possibly in light of capacity constraints.
Mr Van De Weg has his eyes on US expansion, but also has no immediate plans to increase US operations beyond its service to Los Angeles. He said: “We will look at mid-2027 to eventually add an additional gateway in the US.”
However, while recent agreements have opened the door to more cross-border cargo flights, there is still a chance the process could get derailed.
The US Federal Aviation Administration is due to review Mexico’s aviation safety again in December. At the end of the last review, it flagged 21 issues that required addressing by aviation regulator AFAC.
The budget proposal for the agency for the coming year [ Mexican aviation alarmed as AFAC faces 73% budget cut – The Loadstar ] caused alarm in the industry when unveiled last month, but the government has made adjustments. On Monday, transport minister Jesus Antonio Esteva announced that AFAC would get a significant budget increase, plus 100 new staff.
According to him, the administration plans to publish an updated national aviation policy in the coming weeks, and is working on a national air navigation plan covering the years to 2040.

Humanoid robots aren’t ready to juice up the massive, 240-tonne electric haul trucks Fortescue is putting to work in Australia’s punishing Pilbara. Instead, the company is using specially modified and massively powerful automotive assembly-line robots from KUKA to wrangle the massive cables needed to deliver a mind-bending 6 MW of power to its trucks’ batteries.
While Chinese car brands capable of 2 MW “ flash charging ” are making headlines these days, Fortescue and Liebherr have been quietly working together to develop a 6MW charging system for their massive , ultra heavy-duty mining rigs since 2024 – but details about how the process actually works have been scarce.
Until now, that is. In a new video released by the company earlier this month, Fortescue explains how it delivers what amounts a controlled lightning bolt into the battery of its specially developed, 264 (short) ton Liebherr T264E electric haul truck . And, because the massive, liquid-cooled copper cables are too big, too heavy, and too dangerous for any human to handle, of course they’re using robots to get the job done.
“The challenge with a six megawatt charger is that nobody makes these, and therefore nobody makes a lot of the components, either,” says a Fortescue representative, in the video. “So, we’ve had to take systems and subsystems from different industries were using industrial robots that would normally be used for welding in a car factory.”
Advertisement - scroll for more content
A little help, please
KUKA robot charger; via Fortescue.
Fortescue was able to develop and refine its KUKA robots with help from a $10 million (AUD) grant from the Australian Renewable Energy Agency (ARENA), which were earmarked to help the company develop a six megawatt (MW) fast charger test unit and support its ultimate goal of achieving true net zero operations by 2030 .
“Leveraging our world-class capability in battery and charging solutions from motorsport, the fast chargers have been developed for the challenging conditions of the Pilbara,” explained Fortescue Zero’s then-Chief Executive Officer, Ellie Coates , when the grant was announced in 2024. “Equipped with robotic connection options, they will be able to power Fortescue’s future 240-tonne Liebherr T 264 battery electric trucks in just 30 minutes.”
The Liebherr T264E packs an impossibly large 3.2 MWh (3,200 kWh) battery pack – the equivalent capacity of about 40 road-going Tesla Model Y crossovers – to put that 30 minute spec into context. Before you ask, the 'New Nissan Stadium' is the future home of the Tennessee Titans, in Nashville, Tennessee. It cost approximately $2.1 billion and boasts a capacity of roughly 60,000. This is an enclosed, climate-controlled stadium, unlike the existing Nissan Stadium which opened back in 1999. The new arena will host not only NFL games but also concerts, major college sporting events, and yes, even a future Super Bowl.
While the new stadium is scheduled to open in 2027, the Titans won't move in until the 2027 season kicks off, which means they might want to settle in some time during next summer.
What about the Super Bowl? Well, Super Bowl LXIV will take place at the new Nissan Stadium on Sunday, February 10, 2030. Save the date.
While there, visitors will be able to take in the so-called Infiniti Club, a new premium hospitality area within the stadium. It's located along the south sideline within the lower-level seating bowl, and can accommodate up to 3,000 guests, making it one of the largest hospitality areas in American sports .

The Titans are not off to a good start in their 2026 campaign. Norfolk Southern reported higher third-quarter earnings and record revenue Thursday as freight volume grew and fuel surcharges increased, although expenses consumed a larger share of revenue.
The railroad (NYSE: NSC ) said revenue rose 14%, to $3.5 billion, on a 3% increase in volume. Higher fuel surcharges accounted for eight percentage points of revenue growth. Income from railway operations increased 5%, to approximately $1.2 billion, while diluted earnings per share rose 7%, to $3.37.
Adjusted earnings per share increased 10%, to $3.62, excluding merger-related expenses and effects of the East Palestine derailment, along with restructuring and other charges in the year-earlier comparison. Adjusted operating income rose 7%, to approximately $1.2 billion.
Despite the earnings growth, Norfolk Southern’s operating ratio, a key indicator of efficiency, worsened 2.8 percentage points, to 67.4%. Its adjusted operating ratio increased 2.1 points, to 65.4%, underscoring pressure on margins even as revenue reached a quarterly record.
Chief Executive Mark George said productivity improvements helped earnings, while tighter trucking capacity increased rail’s appeal to shippers.
“Demand for rail service increased during the quarter, as a tighter trucking market highlighted rail’s competitive advantages and underscored the opportunity for a more efficient, capacity-enhanced freight network,” George said in the earnings announcement.
“We remain focused on investing in a stronger, more resilient rail network that can support growth we see on the horizon,” he said.
Why it matters: Norfolk Southern is benefiting from a tighter trucking market, but stronger freight demand is not translating into better margins.

source_document.body:
Einride will test Nvidia’s Alpamayo, a reasoning-based AI driving model, inside the Einride Driver, its autonomous driving system, the company said Wednesday. The Swedish company plans to adapt the model to its own vehicles, routes, and operating data, with a live road evaluation planned for the second half of 2027.
The project extends the collaboration Einride announced Sept. 21 to build its next-generation driving system on Nvidia’s Hyperion platform. Adapting Alpamayo is designed to shorten development cycles and reduce the cost of extending the Einride Driver to new vehicle types and routes, Einride said. Neither company disclosed financial terms.
New vehicle types are already on Einride’s schedule. Einride, DAF, and TNO are defining and testing how to integrate Einride’s autonomous system into DAF’s electric truck platform through 2026, with software integration and commissioning scheduled for 2027 .
Einride had more than 5,400 driverless hours in contracted customer operations across six autonomous deployments in the U.S. and Europe as of June 30, according to its first-half 2026 results . The company tied the Alpamayo decision to that record.
“Our advantage has always been running autonomous freight in the real world, for real customers,” said Henrik Green, Einride’s chief technology officer.
What Alpamayo is built to do
Nvidia introduced the Alpamayo family at CES in January. It described Alpamayo 1 as a 10-billion-parameter vision language action model that uses video input to generate driving trajectories with reasoning traces.
The Alpamayo models “serve as large-scale teacher models” that developers fine-tune and distill into smaller models for their own driving systems, Nvidia said. In May, Nvidia launched Alpamayo 2 Super , a 34-billion-parameter teacher model built to be distilled into compact models that run on DRIVE AGX Thor, Hyperion’s in-vehicle computer. The release does not say which Alpamayo model Einride will use.
The company will post-train and distill Alpamayo on its proprietary operational data. In shadow mode, the model runs live without controlling the vehicle. Its outputs are compared against Einride’s driving planner and human driver performance while existing safety systems stay in full control.
PlusAI also adapting Alpamayo for trucks
Einride said it plans to be the first trucking company to deploy Alpamayo on Hyperion. PlusAI said in March it is adapting Alpamayo for heavy-duty trucking on Level 4 trucks built on Nvidia’s DRIVE AGX Hyperion platform. It expects fully driverless commercial operations on those factory-built trucks to begin in 2027.
Einride’s claim turns on what counts as deploying. Green described the company’s position in narrower terms.
“Being the first trucking company in this engagement gives us the opportunity to help shape the model for freight,” he said.
Nvidia framed the Alpamayo work as exploratory.
“By combining Nvidia Alpamayo and Nvidia Halos safety system with Einride’s real-world freight data and safety engineering on Hyperion, we’re exploring how reasoning-based AI can help trucks navigate complex driving conditions and accelerate development for new routes and vehicle types,” said Rishi Dhall, Nvidia’s vice president of automotive.
Why it matters: Einride is betting that Nvidia’s Alpamayo, trained on its own freight data, can cut the cost of putting the Einride Driver on new trucks and routes. In shadow mode, the model won’t control a vehicle, and a live road evaluation is planned for late 2027.

Roche has ended the development of an investigational CAR T asset obtained in the company’s $1.5 billion buyout of Poseida Therapeutics in January 2025, though Roche CEO Thomas Schinecker made clear on Thursday that the company is not pivoting away from this mechanism overall.
RG6540 is an off-the-shelf CAR T therapy designed to bind the B cell surface markers CD19 and CD20. Roche had been running Phase 1 programs for the asset in systemic lupus erythematosus and multiple sclerosis, according to a company presentation in July. This study has been withdrawn, per an August update to a federal clinical trials database. Roche lists the molecule as removed in its pipeline page .
A Phase 1 study of RG6540—dubbed P-CD19CD20-ALLO1-001 at Poseida—in B cell malignancies has also been terminated, a Roche spokesperson confirmed to BioSpace via email.
“We do believe in the CD19xCD20 CAR Ts,” Schinecker said during a Thursday morning press call to present the company’s third quarter earnings. “We have not stopped working on them. We just stopped working on that molecule.”
Schinecker added that Roche is advancing other molecules from the Poseida acquisition that are also aimed at CD19xCD20 and “are even better.” Roche lists no other CD19xCD20 programs on its pipeline page or in its most recent quarterly presentation.
Roche got RG6540 from its early 2025 takeover of Poseida Therapeutics , for which the company agreed to pay up to $1.5 billion. The centerpiece of that deal is another off-the-shelf CAR T therapy called P-BCMA-ALLO1, now named RG6538. Man Buys New 2027 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1X Coupe for $253,320, Now Wants More Than $278,000 for It

I guess we shouldn't be that surprised about what just happened here. Someone bought this ZR1X for $253,200 and then pretty much immediately listed it for sale at auction, but then refused to part with it despite the highest bid coming in at way over MSRP. The bidding stopped at $278,000, which fell short of the reserve.
So, what's the problem? Well, $25,000 over MSRP is not enough in today's market to land you a still-new ZR1X. This is the hottest C8 Corvette money can buy and these are still fetching nearly $100,000 over MSRP easily. Just recently, a Red Mist example with 1,200 miles on the clock sold for $315,000, which came in at roughly $60,000 over MSRP. And that's the cheapest used ZR1X pretty much anywhere.
Yes, this Arctic White example does have way fewer miles, and while the spec is a bit different, I can still understand why the seller would hold out for more. Perhaps closer to $300,000. Give or take.
At the same time, I also understand why someone would try to land it "on the cheap". It's how you force the market to adjust, and had this sold for only $25,000 over MSRP, it would have changed the ZR1X "landscape" drastically. But people aren't ready for that just yet. Valuations closer to MSRP are coming for the flagship C8, but they're coming sometime next year. Definitely not now.
Anyway, time to take a closer look at the spec on this car, starting with the exterior. Highlights include the removable carbon-fiber roof panel, a rear spoiler, carbon fiber accents, LED headlights, front and rear cameras, plus a set of Carbon Flash 20" and 21" forged wheels wearing Michelin rubber. There's also a front-axle lift system, which is a must in pretty much any supercar - especially one that's been fitted with lower body aero elements.
Meanwhile, inside is where you'll find the Jet Black leather GT2 bucket seats (heated/ventilate), the Stealth Interior Trim Package, carbon fiber trim, a keyless entry system, dual-zone automatic climate control, cruise control, a Bose sound system, sat-nav, a head-up display, and a heated and leather-trimmed steering wheel. In terms of electronic driver aids, you've got lane-keep assist, rear cross-traffic alert, side blind-zone alert, and forward collision alert.
Photo: Bring a Trailer As for the drivetrain, it's as good as it gets by modern-day standards. There's a twin-turbocharged 5.5-liter LT7 V8 unit, working alongside an electric motor and a 1.9-kWh liquid-cooled lithium-ion battery pack. Altogether, they "Voltron" into a 1,250-horsepower monstrosity, which also produces 973 lb-ft (1,320 Nm) of torque. Everything gets sent to all four wheels via an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic and an electronic AWD system.
In a straight line, the Corvette ZR1X can rocket to 60 mph (97 kph) in just under 2 seconds flat (with a 1-foot rollout), and if you're doing everything perfectly, you might just put up an 8.67-second quarter mile time. Good luck.

Emergency Evacuation at Jeep Plant, Production Completely Halted
9 photos
Photo: Stellantis North America | Facebook
The Toledo Assembly Complex plant was evacuated, and production was completely halted following a hazardous chemical release at a nearby transport facility. The spill began on Tuesday evening and led to consecutive shift cancellations and multi-mile safety orders.
The hazardous material leak originated at MC Tank Transport, a bulk liquid chemical storage and transport facility, located approximately one mile away from the Stellantis Toledo Assembly Complex North Plant.
Because the North Plant sits directly on the outer edge of the initial mandatory one-mile evacuation radius, the chemical vapor plume forced Stellantis to immediately shut down and evacuate the assembly facility for safety.
The Toledo Assembly Complex is divided into two main facilities that build Jeep's two most important models. The Jeep Wrangler, in both two- and four-door versions, rolls off the production line of the North Plant. In the meantime, the Jeep Gladiator is built at the South Plant.
In response to the incident, the Toledo Fire and Rescue Department and the Lucas County Emergency Management Agency established two safety perimeters. The one-mile radius was the immediate mandatory evacuation zone originally enforced. A strict shelter-in-place order was issued by the Toledo city government for everyone within three miles of the terminal.
The activity of the facility’s north plant was heavily disrupted. On Tuesday night, October 20, workers on the late shift were immediately sent home as the evacuation order expanded. Stellantis officially canceled both the first and second shifts for Wednesday, October 21.
The South Plant, which produces the Gladiator , was already down and not running during this week, due to an unrelated, planned production pause by Stellantis to align vehicle inventory with market demand.
The United Auto Workers Vice President, Kevin Gotinsky, explained that the union representatives are monitoring the situation to make sure Stellantis puts employees' safety first before permitting them to return to the workspace, as reported by the Detroit Free Press.
The chemical leak paralyzed not only production at the Jeep facility, but also regional transit. All train traffic was stopped along a major North Toledo rail corridor. The shutdown blocked vital freight routes used by major rail lines.
The Ohio Environmental Protection Agency and MC Tank Transport confirmed that the chemical released from the 5,500-gallon tank is glycidyl methacrylate (GMA), a highly flammable industrial liquid, used primarily to manufacture plastics, heavy-duty paints, and specialized coatings.
In the meantime, the strict shelter-in-place advisory that affected roughly 50,000 residents within a three-mile radius has been removed. However, activity at the Toledo Assembly Complex North Plant has not yet resumed. While the general evacuation zone is scaled back, the Jeep Wrangler production lines remain halted.
The risk of an explosion dropped, but the compromised tank at MC Tank Transport was left to vent its remaining gases completely. EPA is still conducting air quality testing around the industrial sector. Stellantis will greenlight production at its facility when the air quality in the area is 100% safe.

What does the upcoming European Union (EU) Battery Passport look like to many energy executives? Another regulatory requirement. Another documentation demand. Another checkbox.
In other words, another headache.
But viewing a battery passport as merely a component of compliance infrastructure overlooks its potential as a key piece of financial infrastructure.
Why? Because second-life batteries have an image problem. Despite their possible remaining value, buyers, lenders, insurers, and developers don’t have enough trusted information to confidently determine what that value is. Buying a used battery without that history is like buying a used vehicle without a Carfax report.
Standardized battery data could make these previously opaque assets easier to value, finance, insure, and resell. In that sense, a battery passport could become the Carfax report for batteries. It may not make the battery more valuable by itself, but it certainly makes the battery’s existing value more measurable and trustworthy.
And that makes a battery passport more of an opportunity than an obligation.
The Biggest Discount on Second-Life Batteries Is Uncertainty
Every time someone asks me how much an electric vehicle (EV) battery’s performance changes with temperature, I’m reminded how little most people know about a battery’s history. Now imagine trying to underwrite one as a multimillion-dollar asset.
Financial institutions have traditionally cast a skeptical eye on second-life batteries, mostly because they don’t have all the information they need about them. For example, without a verifiable, standardized rating, it’s impossible to answer key valuation questions like:
How much useful life remains?
How has the battery been treated?
What operating conditions has it experienced?
How quickly has it degraded?
What performance can a new owner realistically expect?
In other words, a second-life battery is a bundle of unknowns. And when lenders cannot confidently forecast future performance, they have to build uncertainty into their assessment of the asset.
Contrast this situation with the used car market and the availability of Carfax information, which creates a trusted record that reduces information asymmetry.
A Battery Passport Can Turn Battery History into an Underwriting Dataset
The power of a battery passport doesn’t lie in any single metric. Rather, it’s the combination of standardized data points that creates a comprehensive picture of an asset’s remaining economic life. For example, a financially useful battery history might contain things like:
Charge/discharge cycle count.
Rate of degradation over time.
Temperature exposure, including extreme heat and cold.
Time to charge and capacity.
Overall state of health.
Broader performance history and provenance.
The real value comes from bringing these inputs together in one place. With better historical data, institutions can create better forecasts. With better forecasts, they can have more confidence in expected future performance. And with more confidence, they can make better valuation, insurance, and financing decisions.
Why? Because financiers aren’t simply buying “a battery.” They’re investing in that battery’s expected future performance and cash-generating potential.
I’ve seen the difference that information can make in the real world. My team has helped original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) aggregate battery data, ingest and clean telematics, and package that information into passports. And that resulting information has helped dealers market vehicles more effectively, while giving customers greater confidence in what they’re buying.
That’s not just another regulation. Having trusted battery information changes the whole transaction. And if better data can change the economics of a used EV transaction, think of the possibilities as the battery moves into its second life as an energy-storage asset.
Making the Move from Compliance to Opportunity
This is where the conversation around battery passports moves beyond compliance. Compliance may get you into the game, but the competitive advantage comes from monetizing the data and delivering value to customers.
A verified battery history, for example, could support a residual-value model that updates as the battery ages. That model could then inform resale pricing, insurance underwriting, warranty terms, or financing.
Let’s go back to the Carfax business model. Here, a dealer or other intermediary could use a trusted passport or certification to demonstrate that a battery’s key data has been verified. The consumer could receive that information as part of the transaction, while the dealer pays for the service because the certification has commercial value.
The value prospects go beyond the automotive industry. Utilities and energy developers, for example, could use second-life batteries for storage and microgrids. What they need is the confidence that enough useful life remains to justify the investment. Battery passports can help reduce uncertainty and improve capital efficiency.
That doesn’t mean the EU framework will automatically become U.S. law. But global manufacturers have strong incentives to avoid building entirely separate data infrastructures for different markets, making the EU standard strategically relevant to U.S. companies as well.
And companies that build the infrastructure to meet that standard early (and capitalize on it) can establish a stronger market position before the ecosystem matures.
The Battery Passport Is the Foundation for the Second-Life Battery Market
Second-life batteries are full of untapped potential, but the market for them lacks the confidence in how to measure that value.
Carfax’s ability to standardize history transformed the used-car market by making uncertainty more manageable. Battery passports could perform a similar function for second-life energy storage.
Once the market can make battery health transparent, trusted, and standardized, second-life batteries can move from “scary unknown” to an asset class investors actively want to finance.
That’s more than a regulatory checkbox. That’s data as an asset, with all the potential upside that goes along with it.
— Michelle Blakeley serves as vice president, Auto & Industrials at Perficient .

PARIS — The United Kingdom’s Royal Navy has a “serious anti-submarine warfare gap” that weakens the country’s ability to respond to Russia’s submarine and underwater-sabotage threat, a parliamentary committee on defense in the High North found.
The Royal Navy currently has only five Type 23 frigates for anti-submarine warfare in service, compared with a stated requirement of eight, and analysis suggests the number of frigates equipped with a towed array sonar could remain as low as five for the next three years, the Defence Committee wrote in an inquiry report published on Thursday .
Anti-submarine warfare frigates are “critical” to helping locate Russian submarines, both in the High North as well as in British home waters, including to protect the U.K.’s ballistic missile submarines that provide the country’s nuclear deterrent when entering or leaving their base in Faslane, Scotland, according to the report.
“Although new frigates will eventually join the fleet in sufficient numbers, the current fleet readiness picture raises doubts about whether the U.K. could sustain the maritime tasks required in the High North by 2030,” the committee said.
Citing the critical role of anti-submarine operations in the High North, the committee recommended the government ensures no further Type 23 frigates equipped with towed sonar leave Navy service until they’re replaced on a one-on-one basis by the future Type 26 frigates .
The U.K. has ordered eight Type 26 frigates from BAE Systems for the anti-submarine warfare role, with the lead vessel scheduled to enter service in 2028, and Minister of State for Defence Luke Pollard said in June that the program remained on track . Norway said in August 2025 it would buy five Type 26s , with delivery to start in 2030.
Should two of the Type 26 frigates being built for the U.K. instead go to Norway to meet the delivery deadline, the Royal Navy would take until 2037 to meet its requirement for a fleet of eight frigates equipped with a towed array sonar.
“Export success must not come at the expense of the Royal Navy’s own Type 26 frigate delivery timelines,” the committee said. “The government must ensure that naval exports expand industrial capacity and allied capability, rather than competing with U.K. requirements for scarce ships, systems and skilled labor.”
The High North, which the committee defined as the greater Arctic and parts of the North Atlantic, “has become central” in U.K. defense and security concerns, with climate change increasing access to the region, according to the report.
As melting ice sheets and sea ice expose Russian bases that were previously mostly inaccessible, Russia is seeking both to defend those bases as well as project force into the Atlantic and U.K. territorial waters, according to the committee. That threatens NATO supply lines from the United States to Europe, as well as undersea and onshore infrastructure, including the U.K.’s nuclear deterrent.
Lack of a credible under-ice capability means the Navy is less able to contest Russian freedom of action in the High North, which risks forcing the U.K. into a more defensive posture, according to the report. The Defence Committee asked the government to brief panel members on progress towards re-establishing an under-ice capability for at least some of the country’s Astute-class nuclear-powered attack submarines.
The Navy’s ASW frigates and nuclear-powered submarines offer the greatest deterrent against the threat posed by Russian submarines and underwater sabotage, though “unfortunately, they are either aging or too often unavailable due to maintenance issues,” the committee report said.
For the U.K. to lead an effective coalition would require the country to address “glaring gaps” in the availability of its maritime forces, and an agreed plan with European allies to deter and if necessary defeat any aggression in the High North from 2030, according to the report.
The committee asked the Ministry of Defence to provide a classified assessment of the capability gaps in case of a conflict in the High North in 2030 in which the U.K. and allies would operate without U.S. support.
“Royal Navy equipment readiness and platform numbers in particular are currently far worse than the government’s stated requirements,” the report said. “With 2030 identified as a key date by which to be ready to deter or defeat any Russian threat, dramatic progress is required before the end of the decade to improve the availability and capabilities of the U.K.’s Armed Forces for operations in the High North.”
The Royal Navy has a requirement for 13 frigates and six destroyers, but has struggled to meet those numbers, the committee said, with only the five Type 23 frigates and six Type 45 destroyers in service.
With the Northern Sea Route becoming more accessible, Russia may try to turn control there into a monopoly, and the government should prepare options for a U.K. state-owned vessel to transit the route to support freedom of navigation, the committee said. Sailing from Shanghai to Rotterdam takes about 14,900 kilometers via the northern route, compared with 19,500 km via the Suez Canal.
The report raised questions about the U.K.’s Hybrid Navy program to combine crewed and uncrewed vessels, saying the High North is “an exceptionally demanding environment” for autonomous systems, and the concept should not become a substitute for crewed capability before unmanned systems have been proven in harsh Arctic conditions.
The committee recommended the government explain within a year how it will test the Hybrid Navy’s main uncrewed systems in High North conditions before relying on them for operational tasks, looking at issues such as cold-weather performance, resistance to jamming and protection from capture.

The intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) used to build persistent awareness of real-time activity has taken a leap forward due to the Navy’s effort to advance this capability with unmanned surface vessels (USVs). The goal is to detect, track, and interdict potential threats quickly and at standoff distances.
Ben Pinx, Principal, Technology and Mission Solutions, Lyntris
Building this awareness is critical to potential future naval conflicts, especially in the Indo-Pacific region. As adversaries conduct exercises and operations in gray zone maritime environments, maintaining situational awareness helps identify potential threats and decide how to respond to them, said Ben Pinx, Principal, Technology and Mission Solutions, Lyntris .
“It’s easy to see something’s moving, I have dots moving all over,” said Pinx. “Now I need to shoot at those dots or I need to create a weapon-engagement envelope to keep those adversary dots out. That’s the threat scenario that leads into what it would look like if we went to full-scale combat in the INDOPACOM area of responsibility (AOR).”
The key is building a persistent maritime awareness infrastructure that allows the Navy to sense, track and share information with other forces and allies at the speed of relevance. That will require a multi-domain, multifaceted approach to ensure coverage is in place where it is needed to paint an accurate picture of what is happening in a region.
From detection to persistent awareness
Sensing is the foundation of ISR efforts, collecting and sharing data on what is happening within a given sensor’s reach. But going beyond just data collection to understand what is actually happening in a given area creates multiple challenges. Persistent awareness requires enough coverage over time to notice changes, establish patterns, examine anomalies and maintain track continuity after the initial detection.
Jack Zaientz, Vice President of C4I and Autonomy, Lyntris
“It’s very easy for us to say that we’ve got coverage, we’ve got this set of satellites, or we can put P8s in areas that we want,” said Jack Zaientz, Vice President of C4I and Autonomy, Lyntris. “But each one of those has a very narrow aperture. While we can maintain coverage broadly over a large area, we can’t cover any particular spot with persistence. That is a much harder problem.
“For the Air Force that is operating in the air doing the strike, that’s OK. For the Army that is trying to do logistics or the Navy that’s trying to do prepositioning, that’s not OK. They need specific information about the areas they’re operating at a very small scale with a persistent view that is hard to achieve with airborne assets that are on the move and that are limited.”
Solving this challenge requires more assets, but it’s not as simple as adding more vessels to the fleet. Their capabilities are the critical component, and building a sense-and-detect infrastructure that can give operators and commanders the information they need to make decisions requires building awareness capabilities across multiple domains.
It also requires a mindset shift. It’s not just deploying assets, said Zaientz.
“What we want to see is that the Army and the Navy operating there stop thinking about boats as individual task assets, and instead think about the network (of USVs) as its own unit,” he said. “We are going to place a network here. Once you think about it from that command posture, you then start asking the resource question of how do I feed in new small USVs? How do I pull out? How do I manage that network? But the network stays intact, stays robust across whatever the AOR that you’ve defined.”
By thinking of sensing and detection as a network as opposed to individual assets, decision-makers can implement comprehensive strategies to gain better understanding of what is happening in an area. This is especially important in the Pacific, where vast distances make continuous local coverage difficult to sustain. While there is an extensive sensor infrastructure in place, maintaining persistent awareness across chokepoints, harbor approaches and logistics routes remains a challenge, and smaller, more agile vessels carrying ISR and communications systems can help fill in the gaps, said Pinx.
“By extending our sensing capabilities using small USVs where we’re able to go out for 190-hours plus and then loiter in certain areas, it starts taking that giant blue ocean and shrinks it down into more manageable areas of interest so that you can start with situational awareness and then transition from that into the targeting aspect,” he said. “We’re not replacing anything and we’re not supplanting. It is genuinely enhancing and extending.”
Building the maritime awareness network
As previously mentioned, full situational awareness in the Pacific is more than just deploying assets and calling it a day. It is a network operation, and it carries with it the challenges of maintaining and sustaining a network in a hostile region.
Each component of the network has its own needs. Crewed surface vessels and aircraft operate under fuel restraints, so having refueling access in the region is needed. Submarines can only operate for so long before needing to resurface and resupply, so they need a place to dock and replenish. USVs can help with these challenges, but create their own issues, such as potentially being captured and reverse-engineered by adversaries to give away closely guarded technology secrets.
“There’s going to have to be some kind of a balance, which again points to the question of data distribution across the network,” said Zaientz. “Maybe you’ve got a bunch of these units that are attritable, low classification or unclassified that are merely passive data collectors. Maybe there’s a small number that are part of the network that have a more exquisite capability that should have a different set of controls attached to them; those have to be managed. The key element here is how do you have the sensor network be self-healing and self-managing within the constraints of this very hostile territory?”
Beyond that challenge is the challenge of operating USVs. Each crewed ship, submarine and aircraft has a dedicated crew, but it is not practical to have a 1:1 ratio of operators to vessels. Scaling a sensing force requires mission-level supervision: operators set coverage objectives and operating constraints, handle exceptions, and retain authority over mission execution while autonomy software coordinates routine tasks across vessels. When communications degrade, vessels must operate within approved mission parameters, coordinate locally where links remain available, and prioritize reporting as connectivity permits.
USVs can help establish what is expected in a certain area and then identify deviations from that pattern for further investigation or even potential engagement. For example, if boats are going through littoral areas in a certain pattern, they are likely following predetermined routes based on the depth of the water and maneuvering capabilities. If those patterns change or ships deviate from them, USVs can flag them so commanders can make a decision on what needs to be done, up to and including engaging hostile targets.
“You would want something that’s multi-mission so that you’ve got non-exquisite and exquisite USVs out there with those payloads,” said Pinx. “And if you see a deviation in the adversary’s pattern of life, you’re able to adjust for that in a way that a soldier, sailor, airman or Marine doesn’t necessarily have to put a lot of brain power behind it because the boats are adjusting in stride based off the rules of engagement or the mission parameters.”
Collaboration and cooperation
Building an infrastructure for true maritime awareness requires not only cooperation between branches of the US military, but also between the Pentagon and industry. By implementing consistent standards, modular architecture and clear requirements for capabilities, interoperability can be built into platforms from the start, instead of requiring troops in the field – or at sea – to figure out how to make systems work by cobbling together solutions or paging through technical manuals, said Pinx.
Lyntris ’ work spans autonomous maritime platforms, mission-level autonomy and maritime command-and-control integration, giving the company a practical view of the challenges involved in bringing those capabilities together.
“The burden needs to be pulled up from servicemembers and put on the companies,” he said. “The government teams that are responsible for the acquisition and the requirements need to bake that in early and upfront so that by the time it gets down range, it is truly plug and play.”
There are efforts underway to make interoperability consistently available from the start, including open standards, modular open systems architecture and reference architectures from the government that help companies understand exactly what is needed and how it should be built to operate within the larger ecosystem. Standardized interfaces can reduce bespoke integration work and vendor lock-in, allowing proprietary technologies from different companies to operate within a shared architecture. That can make it easier to introduce new capabilities and replace or upgrade individual components.
“Historically, integration was point-to-point between vendors, lots of vendor lock,” said Zaientz. “The business models are based around vendor lock. The Air Force and the Navy who are collaborating on the autonomy government reference architecture – which is intended for air autonomy, but it’s starting to get visibility in the service community – are showing that if you have a consortium-based model, you get everyone together to work out a vendor-neutral set of mission threads and APIs, you can move really fast.”

It was a solid third quarter for Ryder, with improvement in just about every metric compared to the third quarter of 2025.
The numbers have been good enough that Ryder (NYSE: R) raised its full-year outlook for 2026. With three quarters in the books, there’s only so much higher it can go. But the company in its third quarter earnings release said it is raising its non-GAAP earnings per share estimate for the year to $14.85-$14.05. In the company’s second quarter earnings, that estimate was $14.40-$14.80. The non-GAAP return on equity forecast was nudged up to 18% to 19% from a flat 18% in the previous forecast three months ago.
Revenue was up in every sector at Ryder. Its Fleet Management Solutions (FMS) segment, which includes its flagship vehicle rental and leasing activities, rose 10%. Supply Chain Solutions (SCS), a contract logistics provider, saw its revenue rise 9%. Dedicated Transportation Solutions (DTS), which is a dedicated carrier that contracts its service out to shippers, increased its revenue 6%.
Earnings before tax at FMS rose 21%. At SCS they were up 7%. But at DTS , that measure fell 5%, due to what Ryder said was “(reflecting) lower operating revenue and a prior year workers’ compensation insurance benefit, partially offset by cost savings from strategic initiatives.”
Used vehicle sales, which Ryder has been trying to restructure the company so that its earnings are not so tied to that market , were strong nonetheless. Used vehicles sold rose to 5,100 from 4,900 a year earlier. But it was the price where the company really benefited from that market, with used tractor prices rising 19% from a year ago, and used trucks climbing 5%.
Prices were improved sequentially as well. For used trucks, the jump from the second quarter was 6%. For tractors, it was 15%.
Used vehicle sales are reported in Ryder’s earnings as a net cost based on provisions for used vehicle sales made by the company. The figure for the third quarter was a net negative $17 million, wider than the positive $3 million a year earlier and negative net $7 million in the second quarter. That is a benefit to the company to have that negative number larger.
In a rapid note put out soon after the release of the earnings, Citi’s Ariel Rosa described Ryder’s number as “better than expected,” and highlighted the 77% rental utilization rate. The company’s target is 80%, Rosa said.
He added that the $17 million net benefit on used vehicle sales was wider than the expected $10 million.
On the DTS performance which came up short of the prior year, Rosa said he saw a benefit from tightening driver markets. “DTS is likely facing elevated driver hiring costs/wages/bonuses on ongoing driver market tightening, which should drive a partial offset of shippers outsourcing more to DTS,” he said.
Ryder’s conference call is at 11 a.m. Thursday. The company’s stock is up 29.8% in the last year, but is down about 12.5% for the three months up slightly in the last month. The first numbers out of the gate at about 9:40 a.m. EDT showed a positive reaction to the earnings, with Ryder up 5.92%, or $14.22, to $254.53.
